title: Safe premises and home visits
audience: Tutors and education coaches (draft shell, no teaching content yet)
learningOutcomes: Identify hazards at a teaching premises or a home visit and decide whether a session can go ahead safely.
Follow a check-in and check-out routine for each home visit, and make sure someone outside the session knows where the tutor is.
Describe the immediate steps for an injury, a fire or a medical event during a session, and record what happened afterwards.

instruction.heading: Checking the premises before the first session
instruction.body: Before the first session, walk through the room where teaching will happen and the route to the exit. Look for blocked exits, trip hazards such as loose cables or rugs, unsafe power points, heaters or fires that are not guarded, animals that may need to be secured, and any locked or unsafe areas. Ask the client or parent to point out hazards the tutor may not know about. Do not teach in a room where an exit is blocked. Record the check, the date, the name of the person who gave access, and any hazard found and what was done about it.

instruction.heading: Home visits and travel
instruction.body: Before each home visit, send the business owner or a named contact the address, the time of arrival and the expected finish time. On arrival, record the time and confirm the session is going ahead. On leaving, record the time and tell the contact the visit is finished. If the client does not answer, if the adult who should be present is absent, or if the setting becomes unsafe, leave and record the reason. Plan the route and parking in advance, and keep a charged phone with the emergency contact saved.

instruction.heading: Emergencies during a session
instruction.body: In an emergency, make sure the people present are safe, then call emergency services. In Australia the number is 000. Give the address clearly and follow the instructions from the call handler. Whether first-aid training or a first-aid kit is required for the role is UNCONFIRMED in this lesson and must be checked. Once the emergency has been dealt with, tell the business owner, and write an incident record following the steps in NEW-TUT-05.
